label: input k at position 0 or 1
explanation: Fires exactly when the input token is k at one of the first two original positions (t=0 or t=1). On dev, precision, recall and F1 are all 1.0. Magnitude depends on position: k at t=0 always gives the maximum (2.162) and carries about 85% of activation mass. k at t=1 gives a weak activation (about 0.12-0.22 of max) that varies with the preceding token. It never fires on k at t>=2, on any other token, or in the delimiter or copy phases (including when k is fed back as a copy-phase input).

issues: Test split is not exactly perfect. Recall is 0.99994 (2 misses out of 33535 active steps) and mass recall is 0.999998. Both misses are copy-phase steps in L=3 sequences that start with k, where k is fed back as the copy input at step 4, with activations of 0.02-0.03 of max. So the claim that it 'never fires in the copy phase, including when k is fed back' is very slightly overstated, but this is negligible noise, not a systematic class.

Dev profile supports the other claims. All activation is in the original phase (none in the delimiter or copy phases), all of it on in_tok=k, and only at t=0 (85.1% of mass, median activation 2.162 = max) and t=1 (14.9% of mass). Sampled t=1 activations are 0.12-0.22 of max and vary with the token before k, as the explanation says.
Test precision is 1.0 with 0 false positives, so k at t<=1 always fires.
